written: 2026-11-07 (Dubai, UTC+4). Committed, with run_confirm.py, run-confirm.mjs, seeds.py, seeds.mjs, closed_form.py, closed-form.json and evaluate_confirm.py, before any search of this run was drawn. The commit's hash and time are the evidence; the commit is local until the author pushes it.
author: Arhan Canli
why: A hostile review of the 7 November 2026 revision objected that its sharpest new evidence was not pre-registered: (i) arch at the merge commit of pull request 882 and the author's corrected implementation (canlicapital PR 562) held their level where the fixed-variance SPA test did not, each run once in an unregistered check; (ii) the best-of-20 single-series tests were oversized at small lag-one autocorrelations, as Proposition 2 predicts, in an unregistered run; (iii) the joint tests were never run at small autocorrelations; and (iv) Proposition 2 assumes independent strategies. This run confirms or refutes (i)-(iii) on fresh seeds and tests the equicorrelated extension of Proposition 2 against a closed form computed before the run (closed-form.json).

background_unregistered_results.arch_882_check: analysis/v2/arch-882-check.json, 2,000 null searches per family, base seed 20261107: arch882 at block 22 rejected 3.80-6.40% across the nine families (block 8: 4.05-5.95%); the fixed-variance spa_c on the same searches 8.50-17.80% at block 22.
background_unregistered_results.snooping_fix: analysis/snooping-fix/snooping-fix.json, 4,000 searches per design, base seed 20261107: the author's consistent SPA test went from 12.03% (v1 code) to 5.18% (corrected) under negative skew; corrected 4.95-6.15% outside AR(1), 6.85% in AR(1); corrected StepM within 0.03 points of corrected SPA.
background_unregistered_results.ar1_levels: src/config/research/null-zoo-v1-ar1-levels.json, 10,000 searches per level, base seed 20261105: one-sided haircut 5.89%, 7.61%, 10.60% and LET 5.99%, 7.76%, 10.82% at phi = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1; Lo versions 5.01-5.55%.
background_unregistered_results.registered_v2: analysis/v2/evaluation-v2.json experiment A: fixed-variance spa_c 4.21-12.26% at block 8 and 8.59-17.80% at block 22; Reality Check 4.52-6.11% at block 8.

design.common: Skill-less searches (every strategy's true mean zero): N = 20 strategies, T = 504 periods, nominal level 5% (1% and 10% recorded, not tested). Size = share of searches with p <= 0.05.
design.S: Studentization, nine families (iid_normal, student_t4, skew_negative, skew_positive, garch, ar1, regimes, correlated_trials, block_cluster). Python (run_confirm.py; families from analysis/v2/nzpy.py): on every search, arch's SPA at merge commit bbfa879a9575ce126178264ac385417f4647fcc1 of pull request 882 with all defaults (studentize=True, stationary bootstrap, 1,000 resamples) at block 8 and at its default block int(sqrt(504)) = 22, and this repository's fixed-variance spa_c and Reality Check (nzpy.joint_tests) on their own bootstrap at blocks 8 and 22. JavaScript (run-confirm.mjs; families from src/scripts/research/null-zoo/v1/families.mjs): on other searches, the author's implementation as v1 ran it (src/js/snooping-core.js) and as corrected (analysis/snooping-fix/js/snooping-core.js), with the same bootstrap seed per search, block 8, 1,000 resamples: consistent and upper SPA p-values, StepM (any strategy declared superior at 5%) and the Reality Check. 3,000 searches per family in each language (30 chunks of 100).
design.L: Autocorrelation levels. Independent stationary Gaussian AR(1) strategies, unit variance, phi = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1. Joint tests: exactly as in S, 3,000 searches per level in each language. Single-series tests (run-confirm.mjs, the generator and tests of src/scripts/research/null-zoo/v1/ar1-levels.mjs): LET, LET-Lo, one-sided haircut and one-sided haircut-Lo, 10,000 searches per level (10 chunks of 1,000). phi = 0 and 0.2 are covered for the joint tests by S's iid_normal and ar1 families.
design.C: Correlated strategies. x_k = sqrt(rho) f + sqrt(1 - rho) e_k with f and e_1..e_20 independent unit-variance AR(1) series of coefficient phi drawn by drawAr1Search, so each strategy is AR(1) with coefficient phi and every pair has correlation rho; rho = 0.3, 0.6; phi = 0, 0.05, 0.1; the four single-series tests; 10,000 searches per cell.
design.closed_forms: closed-form.json (closed_form.py; no random draws): Proposition 2, size = 1 - (1 - u)^N with u = F_bar_{T-1}(c / sqrt((1 + phi) / (1 - phi))), and its equicorrelated extension, size = 1 - int Phi((c' - sqrt(rho) z) / sqrt(1 - rho))^N phi(z) dz with c' = Phi_bar^{-1}(u), c the test's i.i.d. cutoff (LET: Sidak; haircut: Bonferroni). Predicted 5% sizes (LET / haircut): rho 0: 5.89/5.76, 7.45/7.30, 10.70/10.50 at phi 0.02, 0.05, 0.1; rho 0.3: 4.24/4.15, 6.13/6.02, 8.53/8.38 at phi 0, 0.05, 0.1; rho 0.6: 2.83/2.77, 4.02/3.94, 5.51/5.42.

seeds.python: numpy PCG64 via SeedSequence([20261108, experiment (21 = S, 22 = L), cell, chunk]); the arch and nzpy bootstrap seeds are drawn from the same stream. Earlier numpy runs used first words 20261007-20261012 and 20261107 (seeds.py lists them and stops the run if 20261108 is among them).
seeds.javascript: xoshiro128** seeded by splitmix32 with seed (20261108 + experiment * 100000007 + cell * 1000033 + chunk * 7927) mod 2^32; seeds.mjs stops the run if any of its 450 seeds equals a top-level seed of v0, the extended run, the bootstrap-resolution run, v1, v1b, the autocorrelation levels or the snooping-fix check.
seeds.smoke_tests: Before the full run, both scripts are run once with base seed 1 and one round of chunks (Python) or one-tenth of the rounds (JavaScript) to check that they run; those outputs are discarded and not reported. A fix to the code found that way is committed separately and listed as a deviation.

workers_and_stopping: At most 12 worker processes or threads; the Python and JavaScript parts run one after the other, each with 12 workers and BLAS/OpenMP threads set to 1. Each part stops at 85 minutes: work is dispatched round by round (chunk 0 of every cell, then chunk 1, ...), and on stopping only the rounds finished in every cell of an experiment are kept, so a shortened run has the same number of searches in every cell of that experiment and the number is set by time, not by results. Every hypothesis is then scored on the searches kept, with Monte Carlo errors computed from them.
software: Python 3.12, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, arch 8.0.1.dev102+gbbfa879a9 (installed from git at the merge commit); Node 24.19.0.

hypotheses.statement: arch882 at block 8: size <= 0.065 in each of the nine families.
arch882 at its default block 22: size <= 0.070 in each of the nine families.
On the same searches at block 22, the fixed-variance spa_c's size exceeds arch882's by at least 0.020 in each of the nine families.

The author's corrected consistent SPA test: size <= 0.065 in each of the six families without cross-sectional or serial correlation (iid_normal, student_t4, skew_negative, skew_positive, garch, regimes).
On the same searches, the author's corrected consistent SPA test and the Reality Check differ in size by at most 0.010 in each of the nine families.

Negative skew: the v1 implementation's consistent SPA test and the fixed-variance spa_c at block 8 each have size >= 0.10, while the corrected implementation and arch882 at block 8 each have size <= 0.065.

The corrected StepM (any strategy declared superior at 5%) and the corrected consistent SPA test differ in size by at most 0.005 in each of the twelve joint-test designs (nine families, three autocorrelation levels).
LET and the one-sided haircut, which ignore autocorrelation, have size above the upper edge of the 99% band around 0.05 (0.0556 for 10,000 searches) at each of phi = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1.

Proposition 2: for LET and the one-sided haircut at each of phi = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, the simulated size is within three Monte Carlo standard errors (computed at the closed-form size) of closed-form.json's value.
LET-Lo and the one-sided haircut-Lo have size within the 99% band around 0.05 at each of phi = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1.
At each of phi = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1: arch882 at block 8, the Reality Check at block 8, the corrected SPA test and the corrected StepM each have size <= 0.065, and arch882 at block 22 has size <= 0.070.
At each of phi = 0.02, 0.05, 0.1: the fixed-variance spa_c at block 22 has size >= 0.09 and the v1 implementation's consistent SPA test (block 8) has size >= 0.065.

At phi = 0.05 and 0.1, each of the four block-8 tests of H11 (arch882, Reality Check, corrected SPA, corrected StepM) has size at least 0.010 below the one-sided haircut's simulated size at the same phi.

Equicorrelated extension of Proposition 2: for LET and the one-sided haircut in each of the six (rho, phi) cells, the simulated size is within three Monte Carlo standard errors (computed at the closed-form size) of closed-form.json's equicorrelated value.

At rho = 0.6, for LET and the one-sided haircut at each phi = 0, 0.05, 0.1, the simulated size is more than three Monte Carlo standard errors (computed at the simulated size) below Proposition 2's independent-strategy value: the independence formula overstates the size of correlated searches.

bars_rationale: The bars on calibrated tests (0.065 at block 8, 0.070 at block 22) are the ones v2 used for 'close to the level' (P4, P5), loosened at block 22 because every block-bootstrap test, the Reality Check included, was mildly liberal there in v2b's experiment E. The bars on oversized tests are below every earlier estimate by at least two of this run's standard errors (about 0.004 at 5% for 3,000 searches). H8-H10 and H14-H15 use Monte Carlo standard errors so that they test the closed forms rather than a rounded number.
reporting: Every hypothesis and every one of its checks is reported in the paper, held or not, together with all sizes; nothing in this file or in the committed analysis code is changed after the run. Any analysis added after the run is labelled exploratory. evaluate_confirm.py scores the hypotheses from results-py.json, results-js.json and closed-form.json and writes evaluation-confirm.json.
